content.content: [{"id":"sec-p0000","heading":"MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT","level":1,"paragraphCount":2},{"id":"sec-1","number":"1","heading":"DEFINITIONS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.1","number":"1.1","heading":"“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.2","number":"1.2","heading":"“Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.3","number":"1.3","heading":"“Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.4","number":"1.4","heading":"“Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.5","number":"1.5","heading":"“Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.6","number":"1.6","heading":"“Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.7","number":"1.7","heading":"“Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.8","number":"1.8","heading":"“Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2","number":"2","heading":"AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.1","number":"2.1","heading":"Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.2","number":"2.2","heading":"Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.3","number":"2.3","heading":"Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-3","number":"3","heading":"SERVICES AND PERFORMANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-3.1","number":"3.1","heading":"Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-4","number":"4","heading":"ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-4.1","number":"4.1","heading":"An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5","number":"5","heading":"IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5.1","number":"5.1","heading":"Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6","number":"6","heading":"ACCEPTANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.1","number":"6.1","heading":"Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.2","number":"6.2","heading":"If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7","number":"7","heading":"FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.1","number":"7.1","heading":"Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2","number":"7.2","heading":"Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2-2","number":"7.2","heading":"Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.3","number":"7.3","heading":"Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.4","number":"7.4","heading":"Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.5","number":"7.5","heading":"Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8","number":"8","heading":"TERM AND RENEWAL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.1","number":"8.1","heading":"This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.2","number":"8.2","heading":"Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.3","number":"8.3","heading":"On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9","number":"9","heading":"TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.1","number":"9.1","heading":"Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.2","number":"9.2","heading":"Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.3","number":"9.3","heading":"Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.5","number":"9.5","heading":"Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10","number":"10","heading":"EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.1","number":"10.1","heading":"On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.2","number":"10.2","heading":"Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12","number":"12","heading":"CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.3","number":"12.3","heading":"Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4","number":"12.4","heading":"Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4-2","number":"12.4","heading":"During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13","number":"13","heading":"ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.1","number":"13.1","heading":"Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.2","number":"13.2","heading":"For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.3","number":"13.3","heading":"Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.4","number":"13.4","heading":"Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14","number":"14","heading":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.1","number":"14.1","heading":"As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.2","number":"14.2","heading":"Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15","number":"15","heading":"CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.1","number":"15.1","heading":"Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.2","number":"15.2","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.2","number":"17.2","heading":"Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.4","number":"19.4","heading":"For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21","number":"21","heading":"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.1","number":"21.1","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. input.summary: Insert missing Vendor indemnity as new Section 20 and repair the broken cross-reference in 9.3
input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no indemnification section even though Sections 9.3, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one exists (9.3 cross-refers to Section 20.5). We have inserted our standard Vendor indemnity covering IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data incidents and wilful misconduct, with the usual notice/control procedure and IP remedies; per Section 21.3 indemnification obligations sit outside the liability cap.

ops.text: INDEMNIFICATION

Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor against third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. The indemnified Party shall give prompt written notice of a claim, the indemnifying Party shall control the defence with counsel of its choice, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense. No settlement that imposes a non-monetary obligation or admission on the indemnified Party may be made without its prior written consent.

If an infringement claim is made or reasonably anticipated, Vendor shall at its expense procure the necessary rights, or modify or replace the affected Services or Deliverables with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing alternative; if none is reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees and Fees paid for affected Deliverables.

input.summary: Delete the 24-month worldwide non-compete on Customer
input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the products or services we may develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted this clause; it also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no non-compete commitment.

input.summary: Delete the disclose-and-match precondition to engaging another provider
input.comment: [Playbook] We must remain free to buy from other suppliers, and conditioning that freedom on disclosing and matching offers is a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal; we have deleted it, consistent with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment.

input.summary: Delete the MFN running against Customer
input.comment: [Playbook] An MFN in our favour is welcome, but we do not accept an obligation to disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit; we have struck it and rely on Section 12.3's no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement.

input.summary: Narrow the non-solicit to a mutual, 12-month restriction on involved personnel with advertising carve-out and no no-hire
input.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept one-way no-hire provisions; we have made the restriction mutual, limited it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months, and added the standard general-advertising and unsolicited-applicant carve-out (which Section 12.3 already preserves).

ops.oldText: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: 12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement in the Services, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other Party who was directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This Section does not restrict either Party from hiring a person who responds to a general advertisement or other general recruitment effort not targeted at the other Party's personnel, or who approaches the hiring Party on an unsolicited basis.

input.summary: Add a Customer-only termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives us no right to exit a three-year term without cause (the numbering even skips 9.4), so we have added a Customer convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; Vendor takes no reciprocal mid-term exit.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination charge, or further volume or payment obligation, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

input.summary: Replace Singapore law/venue with New York law, aligning with Section 28.2
input.comment: [Playbook] Our accepted governing laws are New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales, and Section 28.1 also directly conflicts with the exclusive New York County venue in Section 28.2; we have changed the governing law to New York and left 28.2 to govern venue.

ops.oldText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
ops.newText: This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

input.summary: Flip Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; delete the revocable term licence
input.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so Vendor assigns each Deliverable to us; Vendor keeps its pre-existing Vendor Technology under Section 14.3 with the perpetual licence in Section 13.2. Our fallback is Vendor ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables.

ops.oldText: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: 14.2 Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each such Deliverable upon creation. To the extent any such assignment is ineffective, Vendor grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, transferable licence to use, modify, and sublicense the Deliverable for Customer's business.

ops.newText: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase commitment, and Fees are payable only for Services and Deliverables Customer actually orders under an Order Form. content.text:
All eighteen playbook rules have been reviewed and submitted. Summary of our position:

**Critical issues**
- **INDEMN (missing)** — There is no indemnification section at all; the document jumps from §19 to §21 while §§9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all assume indemnities exist (§9.3 even cross-refers to a non-existent §20.5). We inserted a new Section 20 with a Vendor IP/breach-of-law/data-incident/wilful-misconduct indemnity, a narrow Customer indemnity, standard procedure, and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies.
- **IP (deviation)** — §14.2 gives Vendor ownership of every Deliverable with only a revocable, non-transferable term licence to us. Flipped to Customer ownership with assignment (perpetual irrevocable licence as fallback); Vendor keeps Vendor Technology under §14.3.
- **LOL-CAP (compliant)** — §21 is already at our preferred position (mutual greater-of 12 months' Fees / USD 1M cap, full Excluded Claims list, payment obligations excluded).

**High-severity issues**
- **NONCOMPETE**, **EXCLUSIVITY/MFN** — deleted the 24-month worldwide non-compete (§12.4 second instance) and the disclose-and-match clause (§7.2 first instance), both of which contradict §12.3.
- **T4C (missing)** — added a Customer-only 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund; Vendor gets no mid-term exit.
- **MINCOMMIT** — replaced the USD 2M/year, three-year take-or-pay with a 12-month, reducible commitment and true-up.
- **ASSIGN**, **LICENSE** — compliant as drafted.

**Medium/low**
- **NOSOLICIT** — narrowed to mutual, 12 months, involved personnel, with advertising carve-out; no-hire deleted.
- **GOVLAW** — replaced Singapore law/venue with New York law, resolving the conflict with §28.2.
- **RENEWAL**, **AUDIT**, **WARRANTY**, **INSURANCE**, **LD** — compliant.
- **TRANSITION (missing)** — added six months' transition assistance, 30-day data return in machine-readable format, and certified deletion.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Vendor's Master Services Agreement — 18 findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the MSA against our playbook. Eight positions are compliant as drafted and need no redline — limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence grant (§ 13), audit rights (§ 22), auto-renewal (§ 8.2–8.3), performance warranty (§ 19), Vendor insurance (§ 18) and the absence of any liquidated damages payable by us.

Ten items require change. Three are critical:

- **No indemnity at all.** The outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), yet §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all assume indemnities exist and § 9.3 cross-references a non-existent Section 20.5. We have inserted a new Section 20 (Vendor IP, breach-of-law, data-incident and wilful-misconduct indemnity; narrow reciprocal Customer indemnity; notice/control/cooperation; procure-modify-replace-refund remedies), which also repairs the broken § 9.3 cross-reference. Note that the § 21.3 Excluded Claims carve-out for "indemnification obligations" only has effect once this insert is accepted.
- **Deliverable ownership reversed (§ 14.2).** Vendor owns every Deliverable we pay for and we receive only a revocable, non-transferable term licence, so we lose access on expiry. We have flipped ownership to Customer with assignment (perpetual, irrevocable, transferable licence as fallback); Vendor still retains Vendor Technology under § 14.3.
- **No termination for convenience.** Section 9 offers only breach, insolvency and performance-failure exits (numbering skips 9.4), and § 2.1 expressly denies termination rights across a three-year term. We have inserted a new § 9.4: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination charge.

The commercial lock-in provisions cluster together and are mutually reinforcing: the USD 2,000,000 per year three-year take-or-pay (§ 2.1), the disclose-and-match right of first refusal / MFN (§ 7.2) and the worldwide 24-month non-compete and one-way no-hire (§ 12.4). Each contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, minimum-volume or most-favoured-customer commitment. Finally, § 28.1 (Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction) is outside our accepted list and conflicts on its face with § 28.2 (exclusive New York County venue); we have moved governing law to New York and left §§ 28.2–28.3 intact. We have also inserted transition assistance and data return obligations at § 10.3, which the drafted exit machinery assumes but nowhere provides.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | Anchored at § 19.5; new Section 20 inserted; § 9.3 cross-reference repaired | Insert Vendor indemnity, narrow Customer indemnity, procedure and remedies |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Flip Deliverable ownership to Customer with assignment; delete revocable term licence |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 1.5, 21.3) | No redline; carve-out for indemnification takes effect only once Section 20 is added |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | No redline |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Delete the disclose-and-match precondition to engaging another provider |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 1.5 (with §§ 7.3, 27.3) | No redline; our § 9.4 insert states no early-termination charge applies |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.3) | No redline; § 14.2 addressed under IP |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | Delete the 24-month worldwide non-compete |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | Anchored at § 9.3; new § 9.4 inserted | Customer-only convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with Section 23) | No redline |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Replace Singapore law/venue with New York law, aligning with § 28.2 |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Delete the MFN running against us; rely on § 12.3 |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Replace three-year take-or-pay with single-year, reducible commitment plus true-up |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | Narrow to mutual, 12-month, involved-personnel restriction; advertising carve-out; no no-hire |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | No redline |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | Anchored at § 10.1 (see § 16.5); new § 10.3 inserted | Six months' assistance at then-current rates; machine-readable data return in 30 days; certified deletion |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.4–19.5) | No redline |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | No redline |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in our playbook as walk-away positions and must be resolved before signature:

1. **§ 2.1 — Three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Our fallback: no standing commitment; any Order Form commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, ending on termination, with shortfalls handled by carry-forward true-up rather than penalty.
2. **§ 2.1 read with Section 9 — No termination right for Customer.** A three-year term with no convenience exit is unacceptable; our § 9.4 insert (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund, no early-termination charge, no Vendor convenience exit) resolves it.
3. **§ 7.2 — Disclose-and-match right of first refusal.** Operates as de facto exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit. Deletion requested.
4. **§ 12.4 — Worldwide, undefined-scope 24-month post-term non-compete on Customer.** Deletion requested; if Vendor needs protection, we could consider a term-only restriction on one named competing product with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
5. **§ 12.4 — One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees, including self-initiated applicants.** Narrowing to the mutual 12-month formulation above is the minimum acceptable outcome.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Send the redline** covering the three critical items first — new Section 20 (indemnity, with the § 9.3 cross-reference repair), § 14.2 Deliverable ownership, and new § 9.4 termination for convenience.
2. **Group the lock-in provisions** (§ 2.1, § 7.2, § 12.4) into a single commercial conversation and anchor it on § 12.3, where Vendor already acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, minimum-volume or most-favoured-customer commitment. Flag the internal inconsistency rather than arguing the point in the abstract.
3. **Raise the drafting defects** with Vendor's counsel: the missing Section 20, the § 9.3 reference to a non-existent Section 20.5, the skipped § 9.4, the § 16.5 reference to an absent Section 11, and the § 28.1/§ 28.2 conflict. These are best framed as clean-up and should move quickly.
4. **Confirm the governing law swap** to New York, leaving §§ 28.2 and 28.3 unchanged so venue and escalation are undisturbed.
5. **Confirm the § 10.3 exit package** with our technical and data teams — six months' assistance, machine-readable export within 30 days and certified deletion — given the hosted health data at issue.
6. **Hold the compliant sections closed.** We should not reopen §§ 8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22 or 24, and should resist any Vendor attempt to trade them against the items above; the § 21.3 indemnification carve-out in particular depends on our Section 20 insert surviving.
"}
